attempts.summary: Created a LUKS2-encrypted volume on node1 (file-backed at /root/secure.img, unlocked via a root-only random keyfile in /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key, XFS filesystem) that automatically unlocks via /etc/crypttab and mounts at /srv/secure via /etc/fstab at boot without any interactive passphrase. Verified this survives a full node reboot: boot identity changed from deef5424-198c-4c8e-95f2-5cd8c8ea3f8d to 9083360a-2982-450d-8966-e208225253f4, and post-reboot the systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service was active, /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, and previously written test data (hello encrypted) was intact.
